title: SentinelAI decision-support governance and safety philosophy
section: SentinelAI governance and safety philosophy (revision 1) > 1. Role of the system
content:
SentinelAI decision-support governance and safety philosophy | GOV-SAI-001 rev 1 (active) | SentinelAI governance and safety philosophy (revision 1) > 1. Role of the system

SentinelAI is advisory. It recommends one of four actions (no action, test, alarm, abstain) and
explains why. It never operates a valve. Trip authority stays with the safety instrumented system; a
shut-in for diagnostic reasons is decided by a person with operating authority.

title: SentinelAI decision-support governance and safety philosophy
section: SentinelAI governance and safety philosophy (revision 1) > 2. Decision basis
content:
SentinelAI decision-support governance and safety philosophy | GOV-SAI-001 rev 1 (active) | SentinelAI governance and safety philosophy (revision 1) > 2. Decision basis

Recommendations come from a deterministic layer: residuals against the digital twin, a calibrated
probability for each failure mode, versioned limits from the knowledge graph and a cost-based decision
rule. The language model explains that result; it does not change it.

title: SentinelAI decision-support governance and safety philosophy
section: SentinelAI governance and safety philosophy (revision 1) > 4. Human review
content:
SentinelAI decision-support governance and safety philosophy | GOV-SAI-001 rev 1 (active) | SentinelAI governance and safety philosophy (revision 1) > 4. Human review

When the uncertainty interval is wide enough to change the recommended action, the system recommends
the action with the lowest worst-case cost and requires human confirmation.

title: SentinelAI decision-support governance and safety philosophy
section: SentinelAI governance and safety philosophy (revision 1) > 5. Change control
content:

The model, the prompt, the document index and the knowledge graph are versioned together. Every
recommendation records the versions it used.

title: Historical well-integrity events with dispositions and outcomes
section: Historical well-integrity events (synthetic) > Event W07-2023-04: A-annulus pressure drop while producing
content:
Historical well-integrity events with dispositions and outcomes | HIST-WI-EVENTS rev 5 (active) | Historical well-integrity events (synthetic) > Event W07-2023-04: A-annulus pressure drop while producing

- Observation: A-annulus about 40 bar below the expected thermal pressure during steady production.
- Disposition at the time: attributed to cooling after a choke change; no action.
- Outcome: three months later a tubing pressure test failed; a thread leak at about 1400 m was found.
- Label: tubing-to-annulus communication. Label source: confirmed by class-A test.
- Lesson: a low annulus pressure while producing can mean the annulus drains into the tubing.

title: Historical well-integrity events with dispositions and outcomes
section: Historical well-integrity events (synthetic) > Event W03-2024-09: B-annulus rebuild after bleed
content:
Historical well-integrity events with dispositions and outcomes | HIST-WI-EVENTS rev 5 (active) | Historical well-integrity events (synthetic) > Event W03-2024-09: B-annulus rebuild after bleed

- Observation: B-annulus rebuilt from 5 bar to 22 bar within 6 hours after a bleed; extra gas returned.
- Disposition at the time: bleed-down and build-up repeated; gas sample taken.
- Outcome: gas composition matched a shallow formation, not the produced gas. Cement remediation planned.
- Label: sustained casing pressure in B from cement gas migration. Label source: confirmed by gas analysis and log.

title: Historical well-integrity events with dispositions and outcomes
section: Historical well-integrity events (synthetic) > Event W05-2025-02: A-annulus rise after start-up
content:
Historical well-integrity events with dispositions and outcomes | HIST-WI-EVENTS rev 5 (active) | Historical well-integrity events (synthetic) > Event W05-2025-02: A-annulus rise after start-up

- Observation: A-annulus rose to 55 bar during the first 20 hours after start-up.
- Disposition at the time: bleed requested by the night shift.
- Outcome: the twin explained the rise as thermal; no rebuild after the bleed.
- Label: thermal pressure, no failure. Label source: operator disposition only, not verified by test.

title: Historical well-integrity events with dispositions and outcomes

title: Annulus pressure management procedure
section: Annulus pressure management procedure (revision 3) > 1. Scope
content:
Annulus pressure management procedure | PROC-WI-010 rev 3 (active) | Annulus pressure management procedure (revision 3) > 1. Scope

Applies to all A- and B-annuli of platform wells. Describes monitoring, categorisation of annulus
pressure, diagnostic tests and escalation.

title: Annulus pressure management procedure
section: Annulus pressure management procedure (revision 3) > 2. Monitoring
content:
Annulus pressure management procedure | PROC-WI-010 rev 3 (active) | Annulus pressure management procedure (revision 3) > 2. Monitoring

Annulus pressure is recorded continuously and trended against the digital-twin expectation. A
deviation that persists for at least 30 minutes is treated as an observation and reviewed.
Both directions matter: an annulus that is lower than expected while the well is producing may be
draining into the tubing through a leak.

title: Annulus pressure management procedure
section: Annulus pressure management procedure (revision 3) > 3. Categories of annulus pressure
content:
Annulus pressure management procedure | PROC-WI-010 rev 3 (active) | Annulus pressure management procedure (revision 3) > 3. Categories of annulus pressure

| Category | Origin | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Thermal | Heating of trapped fluid at start-up or rate increase | Monitor; bleed only if approaching MAWOP |
| Operator imposed | Applied on purpose, for example during testing | Document |
| Sustained casing pressure | Pressure rebuilds after bleed-down at stable temperature | Diagnostic test and well-integrity review |

title: Annulus pressure management procedure
section: Annulus pressure management procedure (revision 3) > 4. Escalation
content:
Annulus pressure management procedure | PROC-WI-010 rev 3 (active) | Annulus pressure management procedure (revision 3) > 4. Escalation

1. Observation confirmed for 30 minutes: inform the well-integrity engineer.
2. Pressure above MAWOP: perform a diagnostic bleed-down and build-up test (PROC-WI-011) within 24 hours.
3. Pressure at or above MAASP: notify the offshore installation manager; the well-integrity engineer
   decides on a confirmatory pressure test and on operating restrictions.
4. Any external leak at the wellhead: treat as loss of containment and follow the emergency response plan.

Protective shut-in is performed only by the safety instrumented system or by a person with operating
authority. Decision-support tools are advisory.

title: Annulus bleed-down and build-up diagnostic test
section: Annulus bleed-down and build-up diagnostic test (revision 2) > 1. Purpose
content:
Annulus bleed-down and build-up diagnostic test | PROC-WI-011 rev 2 (active) | Annulus bleed-down and build-up diagnostic test (revision 2) > 1. Purpose

Distinguishes thermal annulus pressure from sustained casing pressure, and gives evidence about the
leak path through the volume and type of fluid returned.

title: Annulus bleed-down and build-up diagnostic test
section: Annulus bleed-down and build-up diagnostic test (revision 2) > 2. Preconditions
content:
Annulus bleed-down and build-up diagnostic test | PROC-WI-011 rev 2 (active) | Annulus bleed-down and build-up diagnostic test (revision 2) > 2. Preconditions

- The annulus temperature should be stable. A bleed while the annulus is still heating gives a false
  rebuild, because heating continues after the valve is closed.
- The test is not repeated on the same annulus within 24 hours; the previous result is still valid.

title: Annulus bleed-down and build-up diagnostic test
section: Annulus bleed-down and build-up diagnostic test (revision 2) > 3. Steps
content:
Annulus bleed-down and build-up diagnostic test | PROC-WI-011 rev 2 (active) | Annulus bleed-down and build-up diagnostic test (revision 2) > 3. Steps

1. Record the starting pressure.
2. Open the annulus bleed valve through the choke manifold. Bleed to 5 bar or for at most 60 minutes.
3. Record the gas returned (Sm3) and the brine returned (litres).
4. Close the valve and record the build-up for 12 hours.

title: Annulus bleed-down and build-up diagnostic test
section: Annulus bleed-down and build-up diagnostic test (revision 2) > 4. Interpretation
content:
Annulus bleed-down and build-up diagnostic test | PROC-WI-011 rev 2 (active) | Annulus bleed-down and build-up diagnostic test (revision 2) > 4. Interpretation

| Observation | Interpretation |
|---|---|
| Pressure stays low after the bleed, normal returns | Thermal pressure; no leak indicated |
| Pressure rebuilds towards tubing-head pressure, gas returned | Leak from the tubing near surface, for example hanger seals |
| Pressure rebuilds partly, more gas than expected | Gas entering the annulus, for example through cement in the B-annulus |
| Bleed cannot reach the target pressure | Large leak path; escalate immediately |
| Very little brine returned and the annulus needed a top-up | Fluid lost from the annulus, for example through the packer |

title: Annulus bleed-down and build-up diagnostic test
section: Annulus bleed-down and build-up diagnostic test (revision 2) > 5. Expected returns
content:
Annulus bleed-down and build-up diagnostic test | PROC-WI-011 rev 2 (active) | Annulus bleed-down and build-up diagnostic test (revision 2) > 5. Expected returns

The expected gas and brine volumes for a healthy annulus are taken from the digital twin for the same
operating history, not from fixed numbers.

title: Shut-in communication test
section: Shut-in communication test (revision 1) > 1. Purpose
content:
Shut-in communication test | PROC-WI-012 rev 1 (active) | Shut-in communication test (revision 1) > 1. Purpose

Tests for communication between the tubing and the A-annulus by reversing the pressure difference
across the leak path.

title: Shut-in communication test
section: Shut-in communication test (revision 1) > 2. Principle
content:
Shut-in communication test | PROC-WI-012 rev 1 (active) | Shut-in communication test (revision 1) > 2. Principle

While producing, the heated A-annulus can be above the tubing pressure at every depth, so a tubing or
packer leak drains the annulus. After a shut-in the tubing pressure rises above the annulus pressure
at almost all depths, so the same leak refills the annulus. A healthy annulus cools and its pressure
falls; a leaking annulus rises.

title: Shut-in communication test
section: Shut-in communication test (revision 1) > 3. Steps
content:
Shut-in communication test | PROC-WI-012 rev 1 (active) | Shut-in communication test (revision 1) > 3. Steps

1. Agree the deferred production with operations; the test takes about 22 hours.
2. Shut in the well at the choke and the wing valve.
3. Record A-annulus and tubing-head pressure every 5 minutes.
4. Compare the A-annulus trend with the digital-twin expectation for a healthy well.

title: Shut-in communication test
section: Shut-in communication test (revision 1) > 4. Interpretation
content:
Shut-in communication test | PROC-WI-012 rev 1 (active) | Shut-in communication test (revision 1) > 4. Interpretation

A rise of the A-annulus above the twin expectation indicates tubing to A-annulus communication. A
packer leak below the balance depth can instead show a lower-than-expected annulus. The test does not
locate the leak; a temperature or noise log is needed for the depth.

title: W01 B-annulus MAASP calculation report
section: W01 B-annulus MAASP calculation report (revision A) > 4. Sensitivity
content:
W01 B-annulus MAASP calculation report | WIMS-W01-MAASP-B rev A (active) | W01 B-annulus MAASP calculation report (revision A) > 4. Sensitivity

The production-casing collapse bound depends on the pressure inside the A-annulus. If the A-annulus
loses fluid or is bled down while the production casing has wall loss, the collapse bound can fall
below the spool rating and then governs. The digital twin recomputes this operational MAASP online.

title: W01 maximum allowable wellhead operating pressure (MAWOP)
section: W01 MAWOP (revision A) > 1. Purpose
content:
W01 maximum allowable wellhead operating pressure (MAWOP) | WIMS-W01-MAWOP rev A (active) | W01 MAWOP (revision A) > 1. Purpose

MAWOP is a conservative operating screen below the MAASP. Exceeding the MAWOP requires an immediate
diagnostic and an engineering review; it is the alert tier, while the MAASP is the action tier.

title: W01 maximum allowable wellhead operating pressure (MAWOP)
section: W01 MAWOP (revision A) > 2. Rule
content:
W01 maximum allowable wellhead operating pressure (MAWOP) | WIMS-W01-MAWOP rev A (active) | W01 MAWOP (revision A) > 2. Rule

MAWOP is the lesser of 50 % of the minimum internal yield (burst) of the casing being evaluated and
80 % of the collapse rating of the next inner string.

title: Study notes on US offshore casing pressure management regulation (30 CFR 250.519-531)
section: Study notes on 30 CFR 250.519-531 (internal summary) > 1. Relevance
content:
Study notes on US offshore casing pressure management regulation (30 CFR 250.519-531) | REGN-30CFR250-CPM rev 1 (active) | Study notes on 30 CFR 250.519-531 (internal summary) > 1. Relevance

An example of a regulator making annulus pressure management mandatory. W01 is on the Norwegian shelf,
so these notes are for comparison only.
source: eCFR, 30 CFR Part 250 Subpart E, Casing Pressure Management (public): https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-30/part-250/subject-group-ECFR7cee4c12995e05d

title: Study notes on US offshore casing pressure management regulation (30 CFR 250.519-531)
section: Study notes on 30 CFR 250.519-531 (internal summary) > 2. Content in brief
content:
Study notes on US offshore casing pressure management regulation (30 CFR 250.519-531) | REGN-30CFR250-CPM rev 1 (active) | Study notes on 30 CFR 250.519-531 (internal summary) > 2. Content in brief

Operators must follow the industry recommended practice for casing pressure management and the
additional rules in these sections: how often casing pressure is monitored for each well type, when a
casing diagnostic test is required, how thermal effects after initial production are handled, when
tests are repeated, record keeping, and when corrective action or a casing pressure request is needed.
Where the recommended practice and the regulation conflict, the regulation applies.
source: eCFR, 30 CFR Part 250 Subpart E, Casing Pressure Management (public): https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-30/part-250/subject-group-ECFR7cee4c12995e05d

title: Study notes on API RP 90-1 (annular casing pressure, offshore)
section: Study notes on API RP 90-1 (internal summary, not the standard) > 1. Scope
content:
Study notes on API RP 90-1 (annular casing pressure, offshore) | STDN-API-RP90-1 rev 1 (active) | Study notes on API RP 90-1 (internal summary, not the standard) > 1. Scope

Management of annular casing pressure in offshore wells: thermal pressure, sustained casing pressure
and operator-imposed pressure; monitoring, diagnostic testing, maximum allowable wellhead operating
pressure (MAWOP) and documentation.
source: API RP 90-1, 2nd edition 2021, API webstore (purchase): https://www.apiwebstore.org/standards/90-1

title: Study notes on API RP 90-1 (annular casing pressure, offshore)
section: Study notes on API RP 90-1 (internal summary, not the standard) > 2. MAWOP
content:
Study notes on API RP 90-1 (annular casing pressure, offshore) | STDN-API-RP90-1 rev 1 (active) | Study notes on API RP 90-1 (internal summary, not the standard) > 2. MAWOP

A conservative screen commonly taken as the lesser of half the burst rating of the casing evaluated and
80 percent of the collapse rating of the next inner string. Pressure above it triggers diagnostics and
an engineering review.
source: API RP 90-1, 2nd edition 2021, API webstore (purchase): https://www.apiwebstore.org/standards/90-1

title: Study notes on API RP 90-1 (annular casing pressure, offshore)
section: Study notes on API RP 90-1 (internal summary, not the standard) > 3. Diagnostic test
content:
Study notes on API RP 90-1 (annular casing pressure, offshore) | STDN-API-RP90-1 rev 1 (active) | Study notes on API RP 90-1 (internal summary, not the standard) > 3. Diagnostic test

A bleed-down and build-up test shows whether pressure is thermal (stays low after the bleed) or
sustained (rebuilds). Fluid type and volume returned help to locate the source.
source: API RP 90-1, 2nd edition 2021, API webstore (purchase): https://www.apiwebstore.org/standards/90-1

title: Study notes on API RP 90-1 (annular casing pressure, offshore)
section: Study notes on API RP 90-1 (internal summary, not the standard) > 4. Risk-based management
content:
Study notes on API RP 90-1 (annular casing pressure, offshore) | STDN-API-RP90-1 rev 1 (active) | Study notes on API RP 90-1 (internal summary, not the standard) > 4. Risk-based management

Annuli outside the screening criteria can be managed by a documented risk assessment of the individual
well.
source: API RP 90-1, 2nd edition 2021, API webstore (purchase): https://www.apiwebstore.org/standards/90-1

title: Study notes on IEC 61511 (safety instrumented systems)
section: Study notes on IEC 61511 (internal summary, not the standard) > 1. Safety instrumented functions
content:
Study notes on IEC 61511 (safety instrumented systems) | STDN-IEC61511 rev 1 (active) | Study notes on IEC 61511 (internal summary, not the standard) > 1. Safety instrumented functions

Protective actions such as closing the master valve and the downhole safety valve are performed by a
safety instrumented system designed, verified and maintained to a required safety integrity level.
source: IEC 61511, International Electrotechnical Commission (purchase): https://webstore.iec.ch ; Offshore Norge guideline 070 (free): https://www.offshorenorge.no

title: Study notes on IEC 61511 (safety instrumented systems)
section: Study notes on IEC 61511 (internal summary, not the standard) > 2. Proof testing
content:
Study notes on IEC 61511 (safety instrumented systems) | STDN-IEC61511 rev 1 (active) | Study notes on IEC 61511 (internal summary, not the standard) > 2. Proof testing

Failures that only show on demand, for example a valve that does not close, are found by periodic proof
tests. The proof-test interval directly affects the probability of failure on demand.
source: IEC 61511, International Electrotechnical Commission (purchase): https://webstore.iec.ch ; Offshore Norge guideline 070 (free): https://www.offshorenorge.no

title: Study notes on IEC 61511 (safety instrumented systems)
section: Study notes on IEC 61511 (internal summary, not the standard) > 3. Consequence for AI decision support
content:
Study notes on IEC 61511 (safety instrumented systems) | STDN-IEC61511 rev 1 (active) | Study notes on IEC 61511 (internal summary, not the standard) > 3. Consequence for AI decision support

A data-driven model is not part of the safety instrumented function. It may advise, but it does not
replace or bypass the certified trip logic.
source: IEC 61511, International Electrotechnical Commission (purchase): https://webstore.iec.ch ; Offshore Norge guideline 070 (free): https://www.offshorenorge.no

title: Study notes on ISO 14224 (reliability data, failure taxonomy)
section: Study notes on ISO 14224 (internal summary, not the standard) > 1. Taxonomy
content:
Study notes on ISO 14224 (reliability data, failure taxonomy) | STDN-ISO14224 rev 1 (active) | Study notes on ISO 14224 (internal summary, not the standard) > 1. Taxonomy

Equipment is described in levels from installation and system down to equipment unit, subunit and
maintainable item. Failures are recorded at the maintainable item, where repair happens.
source: ISO 14224, International Organization for Standardization (purchase): https://www.iso.org

title: Study notes on ISO 14224 (reliability data, failure taxonomy)
section: Study notes on ISO 14224 (internal summary, not the standard) > 2. Failure vocabulary
content:
Study notes on ISO 14224 (reliability data, failure taxonomy) | STDN-ISO14224 rev 1 (active) | Study notes on ISO 14224 (internal summary, not the standard) > 2. Failure vocabulary

- Failure mode: the observed effect, for example sustained casing pressure.
- Failure mechanism: the physical process, for example elastomer degradation of a packer.
- Failure cause: the circumstance that led to it, for example a material not qualified for the fluid.
source: ISO 14224, International Organization for Standardization (purchase): https://www.iso.org

title: Study notes on ISO 14224 (reliability data, failure taxonomy)
section: Study notes on ISO 14224 (internal summary, not the standard) > 3. Use in SentinelAI
content:
Study notes on ISO 14224 (reliability data, failure taxonomy) | STDN-ISO14224 rev 1 (active) | Study notes on ISO 14224 (internal summary, not the standard) > 3. Use in SentinelAI

The knowledge graph uses this vocabulary: mechanisms belong to maintainable items and cause failure
modes, which degrade barriers.
source: ISO 14224, International Organization for Standardization (purchase): https://www.iso.org

title: Study notes on ISO/TS 16530-2 (well integrity, operational phase)
section: Study notes on ISO/TS 16530-2 (internal summary, not the standard) > 1. Scope
content:
Study notes on ISO/TS 16530-2 (well integrity, operational phase) | STDN-ISO16530-2 rev 1 (active) | Study notes on ISO/TS 16530-2 (internal summary, not the standard) > 1. Scope

Guidance for managing well integrity during the operational phase: barrier monitoring, annulus
pressure management, testing, well operating limits and integrity categorisation.
source: ISO/TS 16530-2, International Organization for Standardization (purchase): https://www.iso.org

title: Study notes on ISO/TS 16530-2 (well integrity, operational phase)
section: Study notes on ISO/TS 16530-2 (internal summary, not the standard) > 2. Annulus pressure management
content:
Study notes on ISO/TS 16530-2 (well integrity, operational phase) | STDN-ISO16530-2 rev 1 (active) | Study notes on ISO/TS 16530-2 (internal summary, not the standard) > 2. Annulus pressure management

Each annulus has a maximum allowable annulus surface pressure (MAASP) based on the weakest element
exposed to it: casing burst, inner-string collapse, packer, wellhead or formation strength. Operating
limits and alert levels are set below the MAASP so that action is taken before the limit is reached.
source: ISO/TS 16530-2, International Organization for Standardization (purchase): https://www.iso.org

title: Study notes on ISO/TS 16530-2 (well integrity, operational phase)
section: Study notes on ISO/TS 16530-2 (internal summary, not the standard) > 3. Sources of annulus pressure
content:
Study notes on ISO/TS 16530-2 (well integrity, operational phase) | STDN-ISO16530-2 rev 1 (active) | Study notes on ISO/TS 16530-2 (internal summary, not the standard) > 3. Sources of annulus pressure

Thermal expansion, operator-imposed pressure and sustained pressure from a leak are distinguished.
Diagnostic bleed-down and build-up tests separate them.
source: ISO/TS 16530-2, International Organization for Standardization (purchase): https://www.iso.org

title: Study notes on ISO/TS 16530-2 (well integrity, operational phase)
section: Study notes on ISO/TS 16530-2 (internal summary, not the standard) > 4. Updating limits
content:
Study notes on ISO/TS 16530-2 (well integrity, operational phase) | STDN-ISO16530-2 rev 1 (active) | Study notes on ISO/TS 16530-2 (internal summary, not the standard) > 4. Updating limits

MAASP values are re-evaluated after any change in well condition, such as wall loss found by
inspection or a change of annulus fluid.
source: ISO/TS 16530-2, International Organization for Standardization (purchase): https://www.iso.org

title: Study notes on NORSOK D-010 (well barriers)
section: Study notes on NORSOK D-010 (internal summary, not the standard) > 1. What the standard covers
content:
Study notes on NORSOK D-010 (well barriers) | STDN-NORSOK-D010 rev 1 (active) | Study notes on NORSOK D-010 (internal summary, not the standard) > 1. What the standard covers

NORSOK D-010 sets minimum functional and performance requirements for well barriers over the whole
life of a well, from drilling to permanent abandonment.
source: NORSOK D-010:2021+AC:2024, Standard Norge (purchase): https://online.standard.no/en/norsok-d-010-2021ac2-2021ac-2024

title: Study notes on NORSOK D-010 (well barriers)
section: Study notes on NORSOK D-010 (internal summary, not the standard) > 2. Two-barrier principle
content:
Study notes on NORSOK D-010 (well barriers) | STDN-NORSOK-D010 rev 1 (active) | Study notes on NORSOK D-010 (internal summary, not the standard) > 2. Two-barrier principle

During production there shall be two independent, tested well barriers between the reservoir and the
environment. The primary barrier is the first envelope that stops flow from the source; the secondary
barrier is the back-up if the primary fails.
source: NORSOK D-010:2021+AC:2024, Standard Norge (purchase): https://online.standard.no/en/norsok-d-010-2021ac2-2021ac-2024

title: Study notes on NORSOK D-010 (well barriers)
section: Study notes on NORSOK D-010 (internal summary, not the standard) > 3. Well barrier elements
content:
Study notes on NORSOK D-010 (well barriers) | STDN-NORSOK-D010 rev 1 (active) | Study notes on NORSOK D-010 (internal summary, not the standard) > 3. Well barrier elements

A barrier is made of elements such as tubing, packer, downhole safety valve, casing, cement, wellhead
and tree valves. For each element type the standard gives acceptance criteria: function, design,
initial verification and how it is monitored in operation.
source: NORSOK D-010:2021+AC:2024, Standard Norge (purchase): https://online.standard.no/en/norsok-d-010-2021ac2-2021ac-2024

title: Study notes on NORSOK D-010 (well barriers)
section: Study notes on NORSOK D-010 (internal summary, not the standard) > 4. Independence
content:
Study notes on NORSOK D-010 (well barriers) | STDN-NORSOK-D010 rev 1 (active) | Study notes on NORSOK D-010 (internal summary, not the standard) > 4. Independence

Elements shared by both barriers (common elements) must be identified, and their failure assessed,
because one failure can remove both barriers.
source: NORSOK D-010:2021+AC:2024, Standard Norge (purchase): https://online.standard.no/en/norsok-d-010-2021ac2-2021ac-2024

title: Study notes on NORSOK D-010 (well barriers)
section: Study notes on NORSOK D-010 (internal summary, not the standard) > 5. Well barrier schematics
content:
Study notes on NORSOK D-010 (well barriers) | STDN-NORSOK-D010 rev 1 (active) | Study notes on NORSOK D-010 (internal summary, not the standard) > 5. Well barrier schematics

Each well has a schematic showing both barriers and their elements for the current well state.
source: NORSOK D-010:2021+AC:2024, Standard Norge (purchase): https://online.standard.no/en/norsok-d-010-2021ac2-2021ac-2024
